1.1.text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is Musi Banyuasin Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Banyuasin. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 5. Office of Women Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers Women Empowerment and Child Protection affairs in Musi Banyuasin Regency. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial (assistance and treatment) protection. 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb. 9. Child with Disabilities is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. I

10.Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in decision-making processes and enjoying changes related to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is implemented with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Abandoned Child is a Child whose needs are not adequately met, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16.Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over that other person, whether carried out within a Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19.Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that are gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. I

24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not engage in activities on the streets so they can grow and develop properly. I

26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to recognize power relation gaps between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of the division of labor based on gender on Women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different. 29.

Article47

(1) The Regency Government may provide safe houses for Women and Children victims of violence.

(2) Safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) aim to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties. I

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for Women and Children victims of violence requiring safe houses include:

a. their life is threatened;
b. rejected by family or community;
c. require intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social I rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article48

(1) Every Woman and Child victim of violence is given spiritual guidance aimed at psychological recovery.

(2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out based on the principles of:

a. not imposing any religion or belief; and
b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim (self determination). (3) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by spiritual guidance officers.
(4) Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of:
a. consultants of the Marriage Counseling, Guidance and Preservation Board (BP4);
b. Officers of the Office of Religious Affairs (KUA);
c. Ustadz or Islamic Scholars;
d. Priest;
e. Minister; and
f. other religious leaders who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness.

Part Two

Health Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence I Article44

(1) Health services for Women and Children victims of violence include aspects: a.Promotive; b.Preventive; c.Curative; d.rehabilitative.

(2) Health services for Women and Children victims of violence are carried out in a manner that is:

a. Comprehensive;

b. accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours;

c. quality; and

d. in accordance with health service standards.

(3) Special health services for Children victims of violence must I prioritize the best interests of the Child.

(4) Women and Children victims of violence are entitled to health I services, including

a. medical services;

b. medicolegal services; and

c. psychosocial counseling.

(5)Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health services as referred to in paragraph (4) are regulated by Regent Regulation

Social

Part Two

Society

Article 10

(1) Society shall be obligated and responsible for implementing the protection of Women and Children including:

a. participation in prevention and providing support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of Women and Children;
b. providing information and/or reporting violations of the rights of Women and Children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervising the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of Women and Children.
(2) The responsibility of society as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Paragraph6

Social

Article 51

(1) Repatriation of victims of violence is intended to return Women and Children victims of violence to their region of origin.

(2) Repatriation of Women and Children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

(3) The Regency Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of Women and Children victims of violence in accordance with the provisions of Legislation.

Article43

(1) Complaints of acts of violence against Women and Children as referred to in Article 42 may be made by reporters consisting of: a.Victims; b.Family;

c. Community; and/or d.community organizations in the field of protection of Women and Children.

(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints: a. directly;

b. by telephone; and

c. by letter.

(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 42 are authorized to handle Women and Children victims of violence obtained through other information.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation

Article 50

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 49 are intended to provide assistance and protection to Women and Children victims of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and legal rights certainty.

(2) Types of legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of BAP; b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office;
c. legal aid in the examination process at court; d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
(3) The Regency Government provides legal aid to Children and Women victims of violence free of charge.
(4) In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3) the Regency Government may cooperate with:
a. Legal Aid Institute (LBH);
b. Women Crisis Center (WCC);
c. Advocates; and/or
d. other gender-sensitive legal assistants.

Part One

Implementation of the Protection of Women

Article49

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services constitute actions by law enforcement officers provided to Women and Children victims of violence and/or witnesses.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

REGENT OF MUSI BANYUASIN,

a. that the government has the obligation to give respect, protection and fulfillment of Human Rights to every citizen including the Rights of Women and Children;

b. that Women and Children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and discrimination and therefore need to receive optimal protection;

c. that the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of Women and Children as well as the improvement of the quality of life of Women and Children, is one of the mandatory affairs that becomes the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regency Government;

d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children;

Article 14

(1) Efforts undertaken by society in order to prevent violations of the rights of Women include:

c. prevention of underage marriage/unregistered marriage. (2) Efforts undertaken in order to prevent violations of the rights of Children include:
a. supervision of various conditions occurring in their environment that give rise to violations of the rights of Children;
b. strengthening the role of community, religious organizations and the family environment; and

Article 50

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 49 are intended to provide assistance and protection to Women and Children victims of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and legal rights certainty.

(2) Types of legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of BAP; b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office;
c. legal aid in the examination process at court; d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
(3) The Regency Government provides legal aid to Children and Women victims of violence free of charge.

a. Legal Aid Institute (LBH);
b. Women Crisis Center (WCC);
c. Advocates; and/or
d. other gender-sensitive legal assistants.

Article 51

(1) Repatriation of victims of violence is intended to return Women and Children victims of violence to their region of origin.

(2) Repatriation of Women and Children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

Health Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence I Article44

(2) Health services for Women and Children victims of violence are carried out in a manner that is:

a. Comprehensive;

General

Article 9

(1) The Regency Government in carrying out its responsibilities, establishes programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children with the Regional Action Plan as the basis for Regional Apparatus in implementing the protection of Women and Children.

(2) Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER III

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article47

(1) The Regency Government may provide safe houses for Women and Children victims of violence.

(2) Safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) aim to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties. I

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for Women and Children victims of violence requiring safe houses include:

a. their life is threatened;
b. rejected by family or community;
c. require intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social I rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article48

(1) Every Woman and Child victim of violence is given spiritual guidance aimed at psychological recovery.

(2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out based on the principles of:

a. not imposing any religion or belief; and
b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim (self determination). (3) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by spiritual guidance officers.
(4) Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of:
a. consultants of the Marriage Counseling, Guidance and Preservation Board (BP4);
b. Officers of the Office of Religious Affairs (KUA);
c. Ustadz or Islamic Scholars;
d. Priest;
e. Minister; and
f. other religious leaders who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness.

I

Article49

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services constitute actions by law enforcement officers provided to Women and Children victims of violence and/or witnesses.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is Musi Banyuasin Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Banyuasin. 4. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial (assistance and treatment) protection. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb. 9. Child with Disabilities is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10.Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Abandoned Child is a Child whose needs are not adequately met, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over that other person, whether carried out within a Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19.Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that are gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. I

24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not engage in activities on the streets so they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to recognize power relation gaps between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of the division of labor based on gender on Women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different. 29.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial (assistance and treatment) protection. 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb. 9. Child with Disabilities is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. I

10.Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in decision-making processes and enjoying changes related to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is implemented with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Abandoned Child is a Child whose needs are not adequately met, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16.Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over that other person, whether carried out within a Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that are gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. I

24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not engage in activities on the streets so they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Public service provider is every state institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities. 30. Community Organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila. 31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their Children, or father and his Children, or mother and her Children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 33. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb. 9. Child with Disabilities is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. I

10.Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in decision-making processes and enjoying changes related to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is implemented with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Abandoned Child is a Child whose needs are not adequately met, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16.Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over that other person, whether carried out within a Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19.Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that are gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. I

24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not engage in activities on the streets so they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to recognize power relation gaps between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of the division of labor based on gender on Women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different. 29.

I

10.Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in decision-making processes and enjoying changes related to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is implemented with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Abandoned Child is a Child whose needs are not adequately met, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Article47

(1) The Regency Government may provide safe houses for Women and Children victims of violence.

(2) Safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) aim to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties. I

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for Women and Children victims of violence requiring safe houses include:

a. their life is threatened;
b. rejected by family or community;
c. require intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social I rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article48

(1) Every Woman and Child victim of violence is given spiritual guidance aimed at psychological recovery.

(2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out based on the principles of:

a. not imposing any religion or belief; and
b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim (self determination). (3) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by spiritual guidance officers.
(4) Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of:
a. consultants of the Marriage Counseling, Guidance and Preservation Board (BP4);
b. Officers of the Office of Religious Affairs (KUA);
c. Ustadz or Islamic Scholars;
d. Priest;
e. Minister; and
f. other religious leaders who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness.

IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part Two

Society

Article 10

(1) Society shall be obligated and responsible for implementing the protection of Women and Children including:

a. participation in prevention and providing support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of Women and Children;
b. providing information and/or reporting violations of the rights of Women and Children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervising the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of Women and Children.
(2) The responsibility of society as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Part One

Implementation of the Protection of Women

Article39

The implementation of protection for Women and Children is organized by Regional Apparatus whose duties and functions are related to the protection of Women and Children.

Article47

(1) The Regency Government may provide safe houses for Women and Children victims of violence.

(2) Safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) aim to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties. I

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for Women and Children victims of violence requiring safe houses include:

a. their life is threatened;
b. rejected by family or community;
c. require intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social I rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article48

(1) Every Woman and Child victim of violence is given spiritual guidance aimed at psychological recovery.

(2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out based on the principles of:

a. not imposing any religion or belief; and
b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim (self determination). (3) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by spiritual guidance officers.
(4) Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of:
a. consultants of the Marriage Counseling, Guidance and Preservation Board (BP4);
b. Officers of the Office of Religious Affairs (KUA);
c. Ustadz or Islamic Scholars;
d. Priest;
e. Minister; and
f. other religious leaders who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness.

I

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is Musi Banyuasin Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Banyuasin. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 5. Office of Women Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers Women Empowerment and Child Protection affairs in Musi Banyuasin Regency. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial (assistance and treatment) protection. 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb. 9. Child with Disabilities is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. I

10.Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in decision-making processes and enjoying changes related to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is implemented with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Abandoned Child is a Child whose needs are not adequately met, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16.Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over that other person, whether carried out within a Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19.Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that are gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. I

24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not engage in activities on the streets so they can grow and develop properly. I

26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to recognize power relation gaps between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of the division of labor based on gender on Women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different. 29.

Article 14

(1) Efforts undertaken by society in order to prevent violations of the rights of Women include:

a. supervision of various conditions occurring in their environment that may give rise to violations of the rights of Women; b. strengthening the role of community, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. prevention of underage marriage/unregistered marriage. (2) Efforts undertaken in order to prevent violations of the rights of Children include:
a. supervision of various conditions occurring in their environment that give rise to violations of the rights of Children;
b. strengthening the role of community, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. preventing marriage at Child age.

Article43

(1) Complaints of acts of violence against Women and Children as referred to in Article 42 may be made by reporters consisting of: a.Victims; b.Family;

c. Community; and/or d.community organizations in the field of protection of Women and Children.

(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints: a. directly;

b. by telephone; and

c. by letter.

(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 42 are authorized to handle Women and Children victims of violence obtained through other information.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation

Article 9

(1) The Regency Government in carrying out its responsibilities, establishes programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children with the Regional Action Plan as the basis for Regional Apparatus in implementing the protection of Women and Children.

(2) Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Paragraph 1

Responsibility for the Protection of Women's Rights

Article 59

(1) The Head of DPPPA must submit a report on the implementation of the Women and Child protection program to the Regent.

(2) The report as referred to in paragraph (1) is submitted periodically once every 3 (three) months.

c. Advocates; and/or

Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb. 9. Child with Disabilities is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10.Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. (2) The responsibility of society as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 61

Financing for the implementation of Women and Child protection is sourced from:

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;

Article28

(1) The Regency Government provides scholarships and/or educational assistance for:

a. children from poor families;
b. neglected children; and
c. children residing in remote areas.
(2) The implementation of scholarship programs and/or educational assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by the participation of the community and community organizations.

(1) The Regency Government in carrying out its responsibilities, establishes programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children with the Regional Action Plan as the basis for Regional Apparatus in implementing the protection of Women and Children.

(2) Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 52

(1) The Regency Government guarantees the implementation of empowerment for Women.

(2) The implementation of Women empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation and Community Organizations.

Article 53

(1) The Regency Government provides skills training for the capacity building of Women.

(2) In providing training as referred to in paragraph (1) the Regency Government may cooperate with training institutions organized by community organizations.

(3) The Regency Government expands access and opportunities for Women in obtaining skills and employment fields.

Article 51

(1) Repatriation of victims of violence is intended to return Women and Children victims of violence to their region of origin.

(2) Repatriation of Women and Children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

(3) The Regency Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of Women and Children victims of violence in accordance with the provisions of Legislation.

Article39

The implementation of protection for Women and Children is organized by Regional Apparatus whose duties and functions are related to the protection of Women and Children.
